name: computer/free-space
title: What takes disk space
summary: See what takes disk space and hand the user the commands that would free it.
when: Use when the disk is full or the user asks what is taking space and how to get it back.
steps: Call system_info and read its disk total, free space and workspace size to see how much space is at stake.
Call run_command with du -h --max-depth=1 ~, piped through sort -h, to find the biggest folders under home.
Call run_command with du -sh ~/.cache/* | sort -h to see which caches have grown largest.
Call multi_command with journalctl --disk-usage, docker system df and snap list --all to measure service leftovers.
Call run_command with df -h and check the free figure agrees with the free space system_info reported.
Write down each large item with its size, what it holds and whether the user still needs it.
If a folder cannot be read or a tool is missing, say so plainly and report the totals you could measure.
Give the user the exact commands that free the space in a code block, each with a one-line note; do not run them.
next: The final answer must show the biggest space users with sizes, how much free space exists, and the exact commands the user can run to free it.
